rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: The FLOW axis that drove yesterday's BTC pick has inverted back toward ETH. Spot ETHER ETFs broke an 8-week outflow streak and turned decisively positive — ~$84M inflow the week ending Jul 11, then ~$96M over three days that pushed ETH to $1,920, plus ~$58.4M on Jul 14 concentrated in BlackRock's ETHA. On top of the spot bid, the STAKING-ETF story is maturing: BlackRock's staked-ETH ETHB (80% staked / 20% unstaked, Coinbase custody) builds a yield-bearing structural demand source that is less sensitive to short-term price swings and rewards accumulating on weakness. Price has confirmed the flow — ETH is the 24h relative-strength leader among majors, outperforming BTC on this bounce (ETH $1,844 vs a soft BTC/SOL tape), exactly the asymmetric 'fresh catalyst + relative strength with a definable stop' the mandate prefers. The complex tape is still Fear (F&G ~25-35, total cap ~$2.19T flat), so the rules say favor a liquid MAJOR — and between the two majors, ETH now owns both the flow reversal and the momentum while still giving lower-beta-than-alt downside protection.
positions.driver: ETH is the correct all-in today: it carries the freshest catalyst (ETF-flow reversal + a building staking-ETF demand base), the clearest relative strength (outperforming BTC and SOL on the current bounce), and momentum turning up (RSI mid-50s, Stochastic elevated). Entry ~$1,844 sits below the $1,900/$1,920 shelf it tagged last week, so the setup is asymmetric: reclaiming $1,900 opens a run at the 100-day EMA ~$1,943 and beyond, while a loss of the ~$1,780 support that pinned it for weeks defines the invalidation. Runners-up rejected: BTC (~$63,978) — still the flow leader on absolute dollars and lower-beta, but neutral momentum (RSI ~51.7, 'defending supports, failing to clear resistance') with no fresh idiosyncratic catalyst, so it offers protection without the asymmetric upside; SOL (~$74.93) — no catalyst, softened again, and has led the bleed rather than the bounce twice for this book. All fills use the verified-fresh feed.
positions.risks: ETH is 'fragile underneath the surface despite outperformance' — the strength is driven by a few large participants and concentrated ETF tickets (BlackRock ETHA/ETHB) rather than broad participation, so the bid can thin fast. It remains CAPPED below key EMAs (100-day ~$1,943) and has repeatedly stalled at $1,900/$1,920; a failure there is a live 'sell-the-news/stretched' setup. As the higher-beta major, ETH falls harder than BTC if the Fear tape (F&G ~25-35) deepens on hawkish Fed minutes, Iran/geopolitical shocks, or a fresh ETF-flow flip — and daily ETF flows are noisy and could reverse back to BTC as quickly as they swung to ETH. Hard stop $1,696.53 (-8%, majors rule) set with wick room below the ~$1,780 support that is the true thesis invalidation — a clean close under $1,780 means the trade is wrong regardless of the stop.
